name: Barack Obama
bio: Barack Obama served as the 44th President of the United States from 2009 to 2017. He publishes an annual list of his favorite books each December.

name: Oprah Winfrey
role: media executive and talk show host
bio: Oprah Winfrey is a media executive and talk show host who built one of the most influential book clubs in the world. Her picks have launched dozens of books onto bestseller lists since 1996.

name: Warren Buffett
role: chairman and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway
bio: Warren Buffett is the chairman and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway and one of the most successful investors in history. He recommends books in Berkshire's annual shareholder letters.

name: Bill Gates
bio: Co-founder of Microsoft and one of the world's best-known philanthropists. He publishes detailed book reviews and annual reading lists on his blog, GatesNotes.

name: Elon Musk
bio: CEO of Tesla and SpaceX and founder of xAI. He has named the books that shaped his thinking in tweets and interviews over the years.

name: Satya Nadella
bio: CEO of Microsoft since 2014, credited with reviving its culture and cloud business. He has described the books behind his leadership approach in interviews and in his memoir Hit Refresh.

name: Sam Altman
bio: Co-founder and CEO of OpenAI. Previously president of Y Combinator, where he ran the startup accelerator from 2014 to 2019.

name: Patrick Collison
bio: Co-founder and CEO of Stripe, the payments company he started with his brother John in 2010. Previously founded the auction software company Auctomatic.

name: Paul Graham
bio: Co-founder of Y Combinator and founder of the ecommerce company Viaweb. Writes the influential essays on startups, programming, and thinking published at paulgraham.com.

name: Reid Hoffman
bio: Co-founder of LinkedIn and partner at Greylock Partners. He hosts the Masters of Scale podcast and wrote The Startup of You and Blitzscaling.

name: Naval Ravikant
bio: Co-founder of AngelList and early investor in Twitter and Uber. His writing on wealth, leverage, and happiness is collected in The Almanack of Naval Ravikant.

name: Jensen Huang
bio: Co-founder and CEO of NVIDIA since 1993, leading it from graphics chips to the center of the AI era. He is the longest-serving CEO among major technology companies.

name: Demis Hassabis
role: Co-founder of DeepMind and Nobel laureate
bio: Co-founder and CEO of Google DeepMind, and 2024 Nobel laureate in Chemistry for the protein-structure work of AlphaFold. He researches artificial general intelligence and how to apply it to scientific discovery.

name: Tyler Cowen
bio: George Mason University economist and co-author of the blog Marginal Revolution, one of the most widely read economics blogs. He hosts the Conversations with Tyler podcast and writes on economics, culture, technology, and food.

name: Luke Combs
bio: Country music star from Asheville, North Carolina, with 19 consecutive number-one singles and multiple CMA and Grammy wins.

name: Jennie
bio: South Korean singer, rapper and actress; a member of Blackpink and solo artist behind the 2025 album Ruby.

name: Keke Palmer
bio: Actress, singer and television host who grew up as a child star (Akeelah and the Bee) and became a widely quoted cultural commentator.

name: Noah Wyle
bio: Actor best known as Dr. John Carter on ER and Dr. Robby on The Pitt; an avid reader who banned phones on The Pitt set and stocked a lending library for cast and crew.

name: Dakota Johnson
bio: Actress (Fifty Shades, Materialists) who runs the TeaTime Book Club, picking literary fiction monthly for readers on Instagram.

name: Jafar Panahi
bio: Iranian filmmaker whose Palme d'Or-winning It Was Just an Accident (2025) followed years of imprisonment and a filmmaking ban.

name: Claire Danes
bio: Actress known for My So-Called Life and Homeland; a serious reader whose O Magazine list named six works that shaped her life and craft.

name: Benicio Del Toro
bio: Oscar-winning Puerto Rican actor (Traffic, Sicario, Che), known for years-long, research-heavy preparation for his roles.

name: Jonathan Groff
bio: Actor and singer (King George III in Hamilton, Mindhunter); spent his nine-minutes-a-night Hamilton downtime reading through his whole list.

name: Ranbir Kapoor
bio: Bollywood actor and avid reader of biographies and autobiographies; he says reading is how he connects with reality, since scripts are fiction anyway.
Novelist and Emory professor whose Oprah's Book Club pick An American Marriage won the Women's Prize. She calls herself a book matchmaker and recommends Song of Solomon to every student.
name: Tayari Jones
role: Novelist, author of An American Marriage

bio: Vermont folk-pop singer-songwriter behind Stick Season. He credits John Steinbeck's sense of place in East of Eden as the model for how he world-builds Vermont in his songs.
name: Noah Kahan

bio: Nine-time Grammy-winning musician, producer and drummer, one half of Silk Sonic, and now a published fiction author: his story collection Peeps on Sunset arrives February 2027.
name: Anderson .Paak

bio: Emmy-nominated actress (Kim Wexler on Better Call Saul) now starring as romance novelist Carol Sturka in Vince Gilligan's Pluribus. She builds characters through what they read.
name: Rhea Seehorn

bio: Grammy-winning R&B singer and actress who plays Hilary Banks on Bel-Air; her debut album Why Not More? arrived in 2025.
name: Coco Jones

bio: Physician-turned-bestselling psychological thriller novelist. The Housemaid (2022) became a global BookTok phenomenon and a 2025 film starring Sydney Sweeney.
name: Freida McFadden

bio: Brazilian actor (Pablo Escobar in Narcos, Civil War) and director of Marighella, Oscar-nominated for best actor for The Secret Agent.
name: Wagner Moura

bio: Oscar-nominated actress (Almost Famous) and Fabletics co-founder who describes herself as a late-blooming reader, won over by John Williams's Stoner.
name: Kate Hudson

bio: American figure skater and 2026 Olympic champion, the first U.S. women's gold in 24 years, after walking away at 16 and returning on her own terms. She winds down from competition with novels.
name: Alysa Liu

bio: Actress and singer (Lizzie McGuire) who also writes YA novels, including the Elixir trilogy and the My Little Brave Girl picture book.
name: Hilary Duff
Alan Cumming
bio: Tony-winning Scottish actor (Cabaret, The Good Wife) and bestselling memoirist (Not My Father's Son); shared his 10 favorite books with the bookstore One Grand.

name: Sterling K. Brown
bio: Three-time Emmy winner (This Is Us, The People v. O.J. Simpson); became a fan of Percival Everett's novels while filming American Fiction.

name: Ethan Hawke
bio: Four-time Oscar-nominated actor and novelist (Rules for a Knight, Indeh); named four favorites on Bustle's One Nightstand in Sept 2026 and six on a One Grand list.

name: Chloe Kim
bio: Two-time Olympic gold medalist in snowboard halfpipe; told Fashionista in June 2026 she loves romantasy and has read all of Fourth Wing.

name: Shirin Ebadi
role: Nobel Peace laureate and human rights lawyer
bio: Iranian lawyer and 2003 Nobel Peace Prize laureate; wrote the foreword to Narges Mohammadi's White Torture.

name: Walter Hood
bio: MacArthur-winning landscape architect and UC Berkeley professor; his interviews cite James Baldwin and W.E.B. Du Bois as touchstones.

name: Victoria Beckham
bio: Former Spice Girl turned fashion designer; told Instagram followers in 2022 she had finished two Matt Haig novels and asked what to read next.

name: Rauw Alejandro
bio: Puerto Rican reggaeton star (Saturno, Cosa Nuestra). No verifiable public book recommendations found.

name: Kica Matos
bio: President of the National Immigration Law Center, named to the TIME100 in 2026. No verifiable public book recommendations found.

name: Zoe Saldaña
bio: Oscar-winning actress (Avatar, Emilia Perez); Junot Diaz sent her the Oscar Wao manuscript before publication and she and her family wept reading it.

name: Ben Stiller
bio: Ben Stiller is an actor, director and producer whose films have grossed over $2.6 billion; he has named formative books in Tim Ferriss's Tribe of Mentors and publicly praised Sidney Lumet's Making Movies and Rachel Maddow's Bag Man.

name: Aliko Dangote
bio: Aliko Dangote is the Nigerian industrialist who built Dangote Group, Africa's largest industrial conglomerate spanning cement, sugar, flour and a 650,000-barrel refinery; no publicly documented book recommendations were found.

name: Scottie Scheffler
bio: Scottie Scheffler is a professional golfer and the world's top-ranked player, a multiple major champion; he says he is not much of a reader beyond the Bible and a daily devotional.

name: Anok Yai
bio: Anok Yai is a Sudanese-American supermodel, the second Black model to open a Prada show; she has named favorite books in a Vogue diary feature and was photographed reading The Count of Monte Cristo.

name: Ralph Lauren
role: Fashion designer, founder of Ralph Lauren Corporation
bio: Ralph Lauren is the American fashion designer who built Ralph Lauren Corporation into a global lifestyle brand; no publicly documented book recommendations were found.

name: Lynsey Addario
bio: Lynsey Addario is a Pulitzer Prize and MacArthur-winning photojournalist and author of the memoir It's What I Do; no books she has publicly recommended were found.

name: Susan Dell
role: Philanthropist, co-founder of Michael & Susan Dell Foundation
bio: Susan Dell is the philanthropist who co-founded and chairs the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation and narrated its Be Well books; no books she has publicly recommended were found.

name: Michael Dell
role: Founder and CEO of Dell Technologies
bio: Michael Dell founded Dell Technologies and remains its chairman and CEO; he named his must-read business books in an Inc. article, from Business Adventures to Physics of the Future.

name: Sundar Pichai
bio: Sundar Pichai is the CEO of Alphabet and Google, who led Chrome and Android before taking the top job; he publicly endorsed Trillion Dollar Coach and has been listed recommending Born a Crime and The Lean Startup.

name: David Ellison
role: CEO of Paramount, founder of Skydance Media
bio: David Ellison founded Skydance Media and became CEO of Paramount after its 2025 merger; he has discussed his sci-fi reading in interviews but named no specific book titles publicly.

name: Precious Matsoso
role: South African health official; WHO pandemic-treaty co-chair
bio: South African health official who co-chaired the WHO negotiations for the global pandemic agreement; former Director-General of South Africa's National Department of Health.

name: Anne-Claire Amprou
bio: France's ambassador for global health since 2022; led the pandemic-treaty negotiations and now chairs Unitaid's board.

name: Lip-Bu Tan
role: CEO of Intel; founder of Walden International
bio: CEO of Intel and founder of Walden International, the venture firm he named for Thoreau's Walden; previously led Cadence's 13-year turnaround.

name: Nikki Glaser
bio: Comedian and TV host (The Nikki Glaser Podcast, Golden Globes host); her reading runs to memoirs, self-help, and relationship psychology.

name: Hilary Knight
role: Captain, U.S. women's national ice hockey team
bio: Captain of the U.S. women's national hockey team and the all-time leading scorer in Women's World Championship history.

name: Vikas Khanna
bio: Michelin-starred chef, author of more than 40 books, and filmmaker (The Last Color); born in Amritsar, based in New York.

name: Lando Norris
bio: Formula 1 driver for McLaren; no public book recommendations found.

name: Mashama Bailey
role: Chef and co-owner of The Grey
bio: Executive chef and co-owner of The Grey in Savannah; 2022 James Beard Outstanding Chef; co-author of Black, White, and The Grey.

name: Matthieu Blazy
bio: Creative director of Chanel from 2025, formerly of Bottega Veneta; a literary designer who has called Kerouac's On the Road one of his favorite books.

name: Dario Amodei
bio: CEO and co-founder of Anthropic; his documented public record is three book recommendations from his 2024 Ezra Klein interview plus The Player of Games, discussed in his essay Machines of Loving Grace.

name: Daniela Amodei
bio: President and co-founder of Anthropic, the AI safety company behind Claude. A former English literature major who reads widely in science fiction and history.

name: Noah Lyles
bio: American sprinter who won Olympic gold in the 100m at Paris 2024. He has spoken openly about depression and is a devoted manga reader.

name: Yiyun Li
bio: Chinese-American novelist, MacArthur fellow, and Princeton creative-writing professor. She reads War and Peace and Moby-Dick every year, six months each.

name: Tony Tyson
bio: Astronomer and chief scientist of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which he first proposed 30 years ago. He pioneered weak gravitational lensing at Bell Labs.

name: Cao Fei
bio: Guangzhou-born multimedia artist whose films and installations speculate on China's urban and technological futures. She collaborates closely with Chinese science-fiction writers.

name: John Furner
bio: President and CEO of Walmart, the world's largest retailer. He started at Walmart in 1993 as a part-time hourly garden-center associate.

name: Jeremy Allaire
bio: Co-founder and CEO of Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin. He reads Camus, Conrad, and Kapuscinski rather than business books.

name: Mari Luz Canaquiri Murayari
bio: Kukama Indigenous leader from Loreto, Peru, and founder of the Huaynakana Kamatahuara Kana women's federation. She won the 2025 Goldman Environmental Prize for defending the Marañón River.

name: Luciano Moreira
bio: Brazilian public-health researcher and CEO of Wolbito do Brasil, the world's largest biofactory breeding Wolbachia mosquitoes to block dengue transmission.

name: Neal Mohan
bio: CEO of YouTube since 2023, after serving as its chief product officer. The Stanford engineer steers the platform two billion people watch daily.

name: Sabrina Walter
bio: Founder of Women for Change, the South African movement whose decade of protests and 1,500 victim stories helped push gender-based violence and femicide to be declared a national disaster in 2025.

name: Dolores Huerta
role: Labor leader and civil rights activist
bio: Co-founder of the United Farm Workers and originator of the slogan 'Si se puede'; at 96, she is the oldest person on the TIME 100 2026 list and still organizing.

name: Reid Wiseman
bio: Commander of NASA's Artemis II, the first crewed lunar flyby in over 50 years; a self-described learner who reaches for books by experts when facing hard problems.

name: Josh D'Amaro
bio: Chairman and CEO of The Walt Disney Company since March 2026 after 28 years in the parks and experiences business; TIME 100 Pioneers 2026 honoree.

name: Mamadou Amadou Ly
bio: Executive Director of ARED, the Senegalese nonprofit pioneering bilingual schooling in Wolof, Pulaar and French; first African to win the Yidan Prize (2025).

name: Nancy Silverton
bio: Chef, baker and restaurateur behind La Brea Bakery and Pizzeria Mozza; a James Beard Outstanding Chef winner whose cookbooks became working references for professional bakers.

name: MrBeast
bio: Jimmy Donaldson, the most-subscribed individual creator on YouTube and founder of Feastables; his public reading list runs to business biographies and company histories.

name: Mariangela Hungria
bio: Embrapa soil microbiologist whose biological-input research replaced chemical fertilizers across Brazilian agriculture; first Brazilian to win the World Food Prize (2025).

name: C.C. Wei
bio: Chairman and CEO of TSMC, the foundry manufacturing the world's leading AI chips; profiled on the TIME 100 by NVIDIA's Jensen Huang.

name: Lauren Hersh
bio: Lawyer and co-founder/CEO of World Without Exploitation, the national coalition against human trafficking; she helped lead the survivor-driven push for the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

name: Rachel Foster
role: Co-founder and President of World Without Exploitation
bio: Co-founder and president of World Without Exploitation, the national anti-trafficking coalition; a New York attorney who has spent 35 years advocating for survivors of the sex trade. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Pioneers.

name: Shannon Minter
role: Legal Director, National Center for LGBTQ Rights
bio: Legal director of the National Center for LGBTQ Rights and lead counsel in the California case that established marriage equality there. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Pioneers.

name: Zabib Musa Loro
role: Founder and Executive Director, Women for Justice and Equality
bio: South Sudanese women's rights activist and founder of Women for Justice and Equality; a 2025 International Women of Courage honoree. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Pioneers.

name: Sarah Friar
bio: Chief financial officer of OpenAI and former CEO of Nextdoor; previously CFO of Square, which she led through its IPO. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Pioneers.

name: Kiran Musunuru
bio: Physician-scientist at the University of Pennsylvania pioneering in-vivo CRISPR therapies, including the first personalized gene-editing treatment for an infant. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Pioneers.

name: Rebecca Ahrens-Nicklas
bio: Physician-scientist at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia who co-developed the first personalized CRISPR therapy for a child with a rare metabolic disorder. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Pioneers.

name: Pope Leo XIV
bio: Head of the Catholic Church and the first American-born pope; an Augustinian friar who spent two decades as a missionary in Peru. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Leaders.

name: Claudia Sheinbaum
bio: President of Mexico and the country's first woman president; a climate scientist and former mayor of Mexico City. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Leaders.

name: Marco Rubio
bio: US Secretary of State and former US senator from Florida; the first Latino to hold the office. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Leaders.

name: Donald Trump
bio: President of the United States, serving his second term; real estate developer and author of The Art of the Deal. Named to the 2026 TIME 100 Leaders.
White House chief of staff under President Trump, the first woman to hold the role; the strategist behind his Florida victories and 2024 campaign.
name: Susie Wiles

bio: Leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party who became prime minister in 2026 after 18 years in exile in London.
name: Tarique Rahman

bio: U.S. senator from Arizona and retired NASA astronaut who flew four space shuttle missions; co-author with Gabby Giffords of books on recovery and gun violence.
name: Mark Kelly

bio: Constitutional scholar, former dean of Yale Law School, and president of the Ford Foundation since late 2025; author of The Democracy Index.
name: Heather Gerken

bio: U.S. Air Force general serving as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff since April 2025; former F-16 pilot and CIA associate director for military affairs.
name: Dan Caine
role: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff

bio: Finnish politician serving as Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for tech sovereignty; former MEP and Finnish education minister.
name: Henna Virkkunen

bio: Argentine diplomat directing the International Atomic Energy Agency since 2019; announced his candidacy for UN secretary-general in December 2025.
name: Rafael Mariano Grossi

bio: Prime Minister of Denmark since 2019, the youngest person to hold the office; led Denmark through the pandemic and the standoff over Greenland.
name: Mette Frederiksen

bio: Mayor of Minneapolis since 2018, now in his third term; governed the city through the murder of George Floyd and its aftermath.
name: Jacob Frey

bio: Turkish economist directing the International Energy Agency since 2015; the architect of its flagship World Energy Outlook.
name: Fatih Birol

bio: Former governor of both the Bank of Canada and the Bank of England, now Canada's prime minister; author of Value(s): Building a Better World for All.
name: Mark Carney

bio: Democratic socialist and New York City's 112th mayor; won office on an affordability platform of free buses, childcare, and rent control.
name: Zohran Mamdani

bio: SpaceX's president and COO, its seventh employee; runs day-to-day operations and turned Musk's Mars ambitions into executed launches.
name: Gwynne Shotwell

bio: Governor of California since 2019 and former San Francisco mayor; entrepreneur behind the PlumpJack Group and author of two books.
name: Gavin Newsom

bio: Real estate developer and longtime Trump confidant; serves as US special envoy negotiating on Gaza and Ukraine.
name: Steve Witkoff

bio: General secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and president of China since 2012-2013; the architect of the Belt and Road and the most powerful Chinese leader since Mao.
name: Xi Jinping

bio: Prime minister of Japan since October 2025, the first woman to hold the office; former economic security minister and longtime LDP conservative who models herself on Margaret Thatcher.
name: Sanae Takaichi

bio: Prime minister of Israel, serving since 2009 after an earlier term in 1996-1999; the country's longest-serving premier, governing through the post-October 7 Gaza war.
name: Benjamin Netanyahu

bio: President of Namibia since March 2025, the country's first female head of state; a former SWAPO liberation activist who joined the movement at 14 and went into exile before independence.
name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah

bio: Mayor of Kathmandu since May 2022; structural engineer and battle-rapper who won the mayoralty as an independent and became a prime ministerial prospect after Nepal's 2026 political upheaval.
name: Balendra Shah
David Senra
bio: David Senra hosts the Founders podcast, where he studies history's greatest entrepreneurs by reading their biographies, often multiple times each. He has covered more than 300 founders since 2016.

name: Andrew Huberman
role: Neuroscientist, host of the Huberman Lab podcast
bio: Stanford neuroscience professor and host of the Huberman Lab podcast, which translates neuroscience into science-based tools for health and performance. Regularly recommends neuroscience, sleep, and behavior books across episodes.

name: Bryan Johnson
role: Entrepreneur, creator of the Blueprint longevity protocol
bio: Entrepreneur who sold Braintree to PayPal and now runs Blueprint, the public anti-aging measurement project. His reading list skews toward science, rationality, behavior, and long-term thinking.

name: Codie Sanchez
role: Entrepreneur and investor, founder of Contrarian Thinking
bio: Codie Sanchez is an entrepreneur and investor who founded Contrarian Thinking, a media company about buying 'boring' small businesses. A former Goldman Sachs and Vanguard finance executive, she wrote the 2024 bestseller Main Street Millionaire.

name: Jason Fried
bio: Jason Fried is co-founder and CEO of 37signals (Basecamp, HEY) and co-author of Rework and Remote with David Heinemeier Hansson. A longtime bootstrapping advocate, he writes about calm, independent company-building.

name: Jeff Bezos
bio: Jeff Bezos founded Amazon in 1994 and led it as CEO until 2021. His annual shareholder letters, which frequently cite books, are studied as management texts in their own right.

name: Lex Fridman
role: AI researcher, host of the Lex Fridman Podcast
bio: Lex Fridman is an MIT research scientist working on human-centered artificial intelligence and autonomous vehicles. He hosts the Lex Fridman Podcast, known for multi-hour conversations with scientists, philosophers, and technologists.

name: Mark Zuckerberg
bio: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in his Harvard dorm room and runs Meta as chairman and CEO. In 2015 he ran the public A Year of Books club, reading and discussing 23 books with millions of followers.

name: Mohnish Pabrai
role: Value investor, founder of Pabrai Investment Funds
bio: Mohnish Pabrai is a value investor and founder of Pabrai Investment Funds, known for openly cloning Warren Buffett's approach. His book The Dhandho Investor (2007) popularized low-risk, high-uncertainty value investing, and his lectures name-drop books constantly.

name: Peter Attia
role: Physician, author of Outlive, host of The Drive podcast
bio: Longevity physician, former surgeon, and founder of Early Medical; author of Outlive and host of The Drive podcast. His reading lists span medicine, biography, decision science, and mental models.

name: Ray Dalio
role: Founder of Bridgewater Associates, author of Principles
bio: Ray Dalio founded Bridgewater Associates in 1975 and built it into the world's largest hedge fund. He wrote Principles: Life and Work, codifying the radical transparency culture he ran the firm on.

name: Ryan Holiday
role: Author of The Obstacle Is the Way and The Daily Stoic
bio: Ryan Holiday is a bestselling author who popularized modern Stoicism through The Obstacle Is the Way and The Daily Stoic. A former marketing executive, he apprenticed as Robert Greene's research assistant before writing full time.

name: Sahil Bloom
role: Author of The 5 Types of Wealth, writer of The Curiosity Chronicle
bio: Sahil Bloom is the author of The 5 Types of Wealth and writer of The Curiosity Chronicle, a newsletter read by millions. He left a private-equity career to write and invest full time.

name: Sam Parr
role: Founder of The Hustle, co-host of My First Million
bio: Sam Parr founded The Hustle newsletter and sold it to HubSpot in 2021; he co-hosts My First Million with Shaan Puri. He now runs Hampton, a community for founders.

name: Shaan Puri
role: Host of the My First Million podcast
bio: Shaan Puri is a co-host of the My First Million podcast and former Twitch product lead and Bebo CEO. He writes a popular newsletter on startups and business ideas at shaanpuri.com.

name: Steve Jobs
bio: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in 1976 and led it through the Mac, iPod, and iPhone eras. He died in 2011; his reading tastes are documented in Walter Isaacson's biography and in his interviews.

name: Tim Ferriss
role: Author of The 4-Hour Workweek, host of The Tim Ferriss Show
bio: Author of The 4-Hour Workweek and host of The Tim Ferriss Show, a 1,000+ episode podcast deconstructing world-class performers. Publishes detailed book lists and runs the Tim Ferriss Book Club at tim.blog.

name: Tom Bilyeu
role: Co-founder of Quest Nutrition, host of Impact Theory
bio: Tom Bilyeu co-founded Quest Nutrition and built it into a billion-dollar brand before its sale in 2019. He now hosts Impact Theory, the long-form interview show on mindset, business, and human potential.

name: Tony Robbins
bio: Tony Robbins is a bestselling author (Awaken the Giant Within, Money: Master the Game) and longtime performance coach whose seminars have drawn millions of attendees over four decades.

name: Ben Horowitz
bio: Ben Horowitz co-founded Andreessen Horowitz after leading Opsware through its acquisition by HP. His book The Hard Thing About Hard Things grew out of his widely read blog on management.

name: Bill Gurley
bio: Bill Gurley is a general partner at Benchmark, where he led early investments in Uber, Zillow, and Grubhub. He writes the Above the Crowd blog and names his favorite books on podcasts.

name: Brian Chesky
bio: Brian Chesky is the co-founder and CEO of Airbnb, the company he started in 2008 with Joe Gebbia and Nathan Blecharczyk. A trained industrial designer from RISD, he credits a Walt Disney biography with shaping how Airbnb storyboards its guest experience.

name: Chris Dixon
role: Partner at Andreessen Horowitz, author of Read Write Own
bio: Chris Dixon is a partner at Andreessen Horowitz, where he leads a16z crypto, and the author of Read Write Own. A former philosophy graduate student turned founder, he recommends books on history, philosophy, and networks in podcasts and interviews.

name: Daniel Ek
bio: Daniel Ek co-founded Spotify in 2006 and has led it as CEO ever since, growing it into the world's largest music streaming service. He reads 60 to 70 books a year and has discussed his favorites on The Tim Ferriss Show and in Tim Ferriss's Tribe of Mentors.

name: Drew Houston
bio: Drew Houston is the co-founder and CEO of Dropbox, which he founded in 2007 after prototyping it on a bus ride. An MIT-trained engineer, he calls Andy Grove's High Output Management the best book on management ever written.

name: Fred Wilson
bio: Fred Wilson is a co-founder of Union Square Ventures, the New York firm behind Twitter, Etsy, and Coinbase. He has written the AVC blog daily since 2003 and posts regular book recommendations there.

name: Kobe Bryant
bio: Kobe Bryant spent his entire 20-year NBA career with the Los Angeles Lakers, winning five championships and a regular-season MVP award. After retiring in 2016 he founded Granity Studios and won an Academy Award for Dear Basketball; he died in a helicopter crash in January 2020.

name: LeBron James
bio: LeBron James is a four-time NBA champion and the league's all-time leading scorer, now in his 23rd season with the Los Angeles Lakers. Since the 2012 playoffs he has read before games to tune out the noise, and his documented picks run from The Alchemist to Shoe Dog.

Lewis Hamilton is a seven-time Formula 1 world champion, tied with Michael Schumacher for the most drivers' titles in the sport's history. He named Paulo Coelho's The Alchemist as the one book he would keep, and shared a Black Lives Matter reading list with his followers in 2020.
name: Lewis Hamilton
Marc Andreessen
bio: Marc Andreessen co-created the Mosaic web browser, co-founded Netscape, and co-founded the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz. He recommends books in long Twitter threads and podcast interviews.

name: Melanie Perkins
bio: Melanie Perkins co-founded Canva in 2013 and leads it as CEO, growing the design platform to hundreds of millions of users worldwide. She has repeatedly named Robert Hoekman Jr.'s Designing the Obvious as her favorite book.

name: Serena Williams
role: Tennis player, 23-time Grand Slam singles champion
bio: Serena Williams won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, the most of the Open era, and spent 319 weeks ranked world No. 1. She stepped away from professional tennis in 2022 and now runs the venture firm Serena Ventures.

name: Stewart Butterfield
bio: Stewart Butterfield co-founded Flickr, then the game studio Tiny Speck, whose internal chat tool became Slack, which he led as CEO until 2023. A philosophy graduate, his public reading runs from management classics and history to the science of psychedelics.

name: Tobias Lutke
bio: Tobias Lutke is the co-founder and CEO of Shopify, which grew out of the snowboard-shop software he built in 2004. The programmer-turned-CEO credits Robert Cialdini's Influence and Andy Grove's High Output Management with teaching him to lead.

Tom Brady is a seven-time Super Bowl champion who played 23 NFL seasons for the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He has called Don Miguel Ruiz's The Four Agreements a mantra for his life and says he rereads it every year.
name: Tom Brady
Vinod Khosla
role: Founder of Khosla Ventures, co-founder of Sun Microsystems
bio: Vinod Khosla co-founded Sun Microsystems and founded Khosla Ventures, where he backs experimental technology bets. He publishes running book recommendations with one-line verdicts on his blog, Medium, and X.
